answer: An AI-agent economy resists sybils through progressive ember-staking on a shared lantern ledger: each identity must continuously burn unique compute cycles to keep its lantern lit, with the burn rate rising for new accounts. A sybil farm attacking by cloning must supply a fresh comet of dedicated GPU hours for every fake agent, because the lantern token is bound to non-transferable hardware fingerprints and expires if the burn stops. The attacker therefore pays linear real electricity and opportunity cost per identity, quickly exceeding any mining reward for more than a handful of clones.
